text:
nora_product: Quick sync 0min 01000 0 - a prospect DP wants a short SLA and clear onboarding checklist before we send invites. Theyre sensitive about residency, retention, and failover.
ben_legal: Can we keep it a one-page addendum? If so I can draft plain-language items: uptime target, deletion window, telemetry access, and route fallback. Need to know if KMS/HSM required.
tia_solutions: They asked for 99.9% and 90-day retention. For pilot we usually offer 99.5% + 30-day default. I'd propose offering a 3-tier retention option (30/90/opt-in unlimited) and a paid upgrade for 99.9% with reserved capacity.
eli_ops: Ops note: hosted pilot = 99.5% realistic. 99.9% requires dedicated or reserved pool. Add planned maint windows (we typically do Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC) and incident ack SLA (1 hour for sev1).
omar_eng: Tech bits: we can support forced KV purge within 72h, and a manual deletion flow for convo logs. Aggregated telemetry dashboards are fine; raw request exports require approved data handling. We can document fallback behavior: route to smaller model variant or rate-limit with notice.
nora_product: Let's keep the addendum tight: must-haves vs negotiables. Must-haves: 99.5% pilot uptime, 30-day default retention, 72h KV purge on request, aggregated telemetry, incident ack 1h. Negotiables: 99.9% upgrade path, raw log exports (opt-in + addendum), longer retention tiers, dedicated capacity.
dp-bot: Reminder: dp-invite-template v4 located at https://redwood.internal/playbooks/dp-invite-v4 - use updated checklist.
ben_legal: Draft snippet for review:
```
SLA ADDENDUM (Pilot): Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide 99.5% monthly uptime for hosted pilot endpoints. Data retention: requests and conversational logs are retained 30 days by default. Customer may request deletion of KV cache and logs; Redwood will delete within 72 hours of written request, subject to any legal holds. Telemetry: aggregated metrics and latency dashboards provided; raw request logs require explicit consent and an approved data-handling addendum. Failover: During capacity or safety constraints Redwood may route traffic to a compatible model variant or apply temporary rate limits; Redwood will notify partner and provide remediation timeline.
```
tia_solutions: Add a single line that lists acceptance criteria we'll use for launch: latency p95 < 500ms, quality regression <= 3% on partner eval set, uptime >= 99.5% during pilot window.
eli_ops: Ops will confirm maintenance windows and put them in the invite. Also propose a one-hour on-call ack and 24h update cadence for Sev1 incidents.
omar_eng: For dedicated/private deployments well call out the 99.9% SLA and reserved capacity commit as the upgrade path. Include simple language: "Upgrade to dedicated reserved pool available upon separate agreement."
ben_legal: I'll post a redline of the addendum and a checkbox onboarding list (NDA, onboarding call, sample prompt set, eval set, POC contact, expected acceptance criteria) by EOD.
nora_product: Action list: ben = addendum + onboarding checklist, eli = maintenance windows + incident cadence, omar = technical deletion & upgrade wording, tia = partner-facing talking points and sample 5-prompt eval. Aim to send invites next Wednesday.
tia_solutions: I'll prepare 5 sample prompts and a short scoring rubric (binary pass/fail + notes) to include.
ben_legal: Will also include short fallback clause: "If a route change occurs, Redwood will notify within 30 minutes and follow up with timeline to restore preferred routing."
eli_ops: Also suggest we include a line about metrics visibility: partners get a dashboard and weekly usage export summary (no raw logs unless opted-in).
nora_product: Perfect. Keep the invite simple  one pager + checklist + 5 prompts. If partner pushes for enterprise SOW we'll escalate. reconvene if redlines diverge. :white_check_mark:
